claims.claim: According to Oxford Reference, the Acts were written by an anonymous friend of the martyrs who was arrested with them but later released.
Marian and James died in 259 during the persecution under Emperor Valerian.
James was a deacon and Marian was a lector.
Oxford Reference says the martyrs were condemned by the legatus of Numidia, probably C. Macrinius Decianus.

The text tells of events in Numidia in spring 259, including the arrest, suffering and glorification of Marian and James, and shows how Roman authorities and Christians behaved in the Valerianic persecution.
Bishops Agapius and Secundinus suffered first, after calling at the writer's house on their way to martyrdom, and their example and encouragement helped inspire Marian and James.
The Passion is the only source that tells of the deaths of the bishops Agapius and Secundinus.

Centurions surrounded the house and made several arrests; Marian and James confessed their faith and their orders, were tortured on the rack and imprisoned, and there received visions, including one of Cyprian who gave them pure water to drink.
